clue.text: Devon, Cornwall, perhaps, long for change?

parts.note: Devon and Cornwall are counties in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A wistful question about whether the far south-west of England is yearning for something new.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon and Cornwall are the two westernmost English counties, in the region called the South West.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to swap one thing for another is to make a change.

clue.text: Hard-nosed quiet wife invested in claret?

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: invested in means the wife is put inside the wine word

parts.note: claret is a red wine, so red

explanation.surface: A tough-minded, silent wife sinking money into Bordeaux wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, so it stands for RED here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hard-nosed means astute and unsentimental in judgement.

clue.text: Unconventional Bohemian taste — sharing problems

indicators.note: unconventional suggests these letters are arranged in no standard order

explanation.surface: An artistic, unconventional sensibility that comes with shared difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: people in the same situation, facing the same trouble, are said to be in the same boat.

clue.text: Cold bird, swindler?

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
a rook is a crow-like bird

explanation.surface: A chilly bird that may be a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a crook is a dishonest person, such as a fraudster.

clue.text: Advice about vessel for Swede perhaps

indicators.note: about means the word for advice goes around the vessel

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: Someone seeking guidance on a container for a Scandinavian person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like a Swedish person; it is the root vegetable, which in Scotland and parts of England is called a turnip.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the swede is a root vegetable of the turnip family, often so named.

clue.text: A French performance, unfinished, Royal Navy cut? No!

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for performance loses its last letter

parts.note: a show is a performance

explanation.surface: A French show cut short, and the navy is asked whether it has been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or wool never clipped is unshorn, the opposite of cut.

clue.text: Northeast answer courteous no end — a pleasing Italian dessert

indicators.note: no end means the word for courteous drops its last letter

parts.note: polite means courteous
nice means pleasing

explanation.surface: A courteous answer from somewhere in the northeast, followed by a lovely Italian pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: layered ice cream in three flavours, named after Naples, is an Italian-style dessert.

clue.text: Balance put in Post Office immediately

indicators.note: put in means the balance goes inside the Post Office letters

parts.note: the rest is the balance or remainder

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay the remaining balance into a Post Office account straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: presto, from Italian, means at once, as in a conjuror's 'hey presto'.

clue.text: Order pies for a stage ceremony

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to commission pastries for a theatre event.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite marking a life transition is a kind of ceremony, such as a coming-of-age ritual.

clue.text: Friend metres off in the evergreens

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of metres are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A friend has wandered several metres off into the evergreen trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: palms keep their leaves year round, so they count among evergreen trees.

clue.text: Seafood fellow found in western lake close to rock

indicators.note: found in puts the fellow inside the western and lake letters

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
he refers to a male, a fellow

indicators.note: close to rock means the final letter of rock

explanation.surface: A man discovered by a western lake near some rocks, with seafood on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the whelk is an edible sea snail sold as seafood.

clue.text: Toilet, unfashionable, king enters — a worry

indicators.note: enters says the king goes into the other letters

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
out of fashion is simply out
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king walks into an outdated lavatory, which is cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the idiom 'that's your lookout', meaning that's your concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: in British use one's affair or concern is one's lookout, as in 'that's your lookout'.

clue.text: Bill, unusually lenient at second game

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of lenient come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Bill, a man named in the clue, being unusually lenient while finishing second in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ping-pong is a game played with bats over a net on a table.

clue.text: This person initially labourer, ultra determined, destroyed industrial textile equipment

definitions.text: This person initially labourer, ultra determined, destroyed industrial textile equipment

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words that follow

parts.words: labourer, ultra determined, destroyed industrial textile equipment

explanation.surface: A description of a determined worker who smashed factory weaving machines.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as spelling it out from first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: History: early nineteenth-century English textile workers who smashed mechanised looms are known by this name.

clue.text: Policeman — one managing to absorb pressure

indicators.note: to absorb means the managing person takes in the pressure letter

parts.note: a coper is someone who copes, or manages
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A police officer who handles stress well.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a copper is British informal for a police officer.

clue.text: Polluted motorway in wet surroundings

indicators.note: in wet surroundings means the motorway sits inside the word for wet

parts.note: soggy means wet through
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A dirty motorway on a damp, miserable day.
explanation.definitionFit: Air full of smog, a smoky fog, is polluted.

clue.text: Late bowling sequence, contest not completed

parts.note: in cricket an over is a sequence of six balls bowled

indicators.note: not completed means the word for contest loses its last letter

parts.note: a duel is a contest between two

explanation.surface: A cricket match running late, with the contest left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something past its due time is overdue, or late.

clue.text: Tea at both ends of room — attractive feature

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea

indicators.note: both ends of room means its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cup of tea at either end of a room makes it more appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a charm is a pleasing quality that attracts people.

clue.text: Preside over Church broadcast

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Overseeing a church service that is being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to chair a meeting is to preside over it.

clue.text: In favour of attacks (running) and distribution of gains

parts.note: pro means in favour of
fits are sudden attacks of illness or emotion
haring is running fast, like a hare

explanation.surface: A supporter of raids and racing, also keen on spreading the profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Business sense: a scheme dividing company profits among staff spreads the gains around.

clue.text: Part of opera: The Ring? Quite

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A query about a section of Wagner's Ring cycle, answered with a polite 'quite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both words mean fairly or to some degree, as in 'quite good'.

clue.text: Eager to get good deer back at end of January

indicators.note: back means the word deer is read backwards
end of January means its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone keen to get good venison back at the end of January.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: avid or keen to have more, as in greedy for success.
